question: Which global campaign was launched in 1987 to bring attention to high maternal mortality rates?
explanation: The Safe Motherhood Initiative began in 1987 to spotlight maternal deaths in developing countries and place the issue on the global health agenda. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h1)

question: How did early global health initiatives change over time regarding maternal and child health?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on hospital-based surgical interventions for all pregnant women
options.B: Abandoning global targets in favor of completely independent local community funding
options.C: Moving from isolated disease programs to broader primary healthcare approaches
options.D: Replacing traditional birth attendants without training any skilled personnel

explanation: Global strategies evolved from targeting single issues to embracing comprehensive primary healthcare that looks at overall social and economic health factors. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which Millennium Development Goal was focused specifically on improving maternal health?
explanation: MDG 5 specifically targeted the improvement of maternal health and universal access to reproductive health between 2000 and 2015. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a major difference between the Millennium Development Goals and the Sustainable Development Goals?

options.A: The SDGs ignore maternal health completely to focus entirely on industrial development
options.B: The MDGs had a 30-year implementation timeline while SDGs lasted only five years
options.C: The MDGs were created by individual hospitals rather than international bodies
options.D: The SDGs apply universally to all nations, whereas MDGs focused mostly on developing countries

explanation: While the MDGs primarily targeted low-income and developing nations, the SDG framework applies universally to low, middle, and high-income countries. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the global target set by SDG 3.1 for maternal mortality by the year 2030?

options.A: Zero maternal deaths globally without exception
options.B: Less than 70 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
options.C: Exactly 200 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
options.D: Less than 500 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births

explanation: SDG target 3.1 aims to lower the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h3)

question: A clinic in a rural community records high newborn deaths in the first week of life. Meeting which SDG target addresses this challenge?
explanation: SDG 3.2 focuses directly on ending preventable newborn and child deaths to reduce neonatal mortality. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why are midwives so important for achieving SDG 3 in low-resource settings?

options.A: They are exclusively responsible for writing national health policies and budgets
options.B: They manage tertiary hospitals and large pharmaceutical manufacturing plants
options.C: They focus solely on administrative paperwork rather than clinical care
options.D: They provide the majority of essential maternal and newborn services where specialists are scarce

explanation: Midwives deliver the bulk of primary maternal and newborn care, serving as the main defense against maternal and infant mortality where resources are limited. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h4)

question: Besides attending births, what else does a midwife do to support maternal health?

options.A: Replacing the need for community health extension workers entirely
options.B: Providing antenatal education and managing timely emergency referrals
options.C: Importing foreign medical equipment and funding local clinics

explanation: Midwives offer full care that includes health education, monitoring pregnancy, spotting complications, and arranging prompt referrals when emergencies occur. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of Universal Health Coverage?

options.A: Eliminating all traditional birth attendants without replacing them
options.B: Providing free healthcare services exclusively to wealthy urban citizens
options.C: Ensuring everyone receives needed health services without financial hardship
options.D: Making tertiary hospitals entirely self-funding through high patient fees

explanation: Universal Health Coverage ensures that everyone has access to quality health services without suffering financial ruin. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which group usually faces the greatest health gaps in maternal and child health in developing countries?

options.A: Civil servants working in federal government ministries in capital cities
options.B: Specialist obstetricians and gynecologists practicing in private hospitals
options.C: Women living in remote rural areas and impoverished urban slums
options.D: Individuals with private health insurance policies and high incomes

explanation: Marginalized populations, especially rural dwellers and slum residents, face severe barriers to quality care, which leads to higher mortality rates. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a primary purpose of health information systems like DHIS2 in maternal-child health?

options.A: Replacing clinical guidelines for diagnosing high-risk pregnancies
options.B: Managing payroll for doctors and nurses working in tertiary centers
options.C: Tracking health service data to measure progress and guide resource allocation
options.D: Regulating pharmaceutical prices across local open markets

explanation: Reliable data platforms help health systems monitor disease and mortality trends so resources can be sent where they are needed most. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h6)

question: A health center fails to record community birth outcomes accurately in its registers. What is the most direct result of this?

options.A: Policy-makers may fail to recognize local health crises and misallocate resources
options.B: The federal government will automatically upgrade the facility to a teaching hospital
options.C: Pregnant women will immediately stop attending antenatal care clinics
options.D: Midwives will receive higher salaries due to decreased administrative tasks

explanation: Inaccurate data hides the true picture of maternal and child health outcomes, making it difficult for planners to target help where it is needed. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T4#BMP322_U2_T4_h6)
